problem.text: The change addresses a tensor-name mismatch by mapping multi_modal_projector.mm_input_projection_weight to multi_modal_projector.mm_input_projection.weight. Previously, header keys were indexed verbatim.

reasoning.text: Normalization belongs in the parsed header as well as the collection index: get_tensor, get_tensor_size and list_tensors use the indexed key to retrieve header[key]. Renaming only the index would leave those lookups inconsistent.

impact.text: The replacement applies globally to the exact matching name, without checking architecture. It changes the in-memory namespace, not tensor shapes, offsets or on-disk bytes; the original spelling is not retained as an alias.

source_notes.text: The root loading-tokenization entry was read. It establishes the existing separation between Python name/offset interpretation and bulk tensor loading, and records limited header validation. Inspection of the parent and task diff shows that this change adds no file-bound or overlapping-range validation.

Issue #33, “Error converting model,” reports file-opening failures and later GLM sampling trouble; issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” reports a padding-size mismatch. Their connection here is inferred only from safetensors.py traceback overlap, not evidence that either motivated this key rename.

limitations: No real checkpoint loading, conversion or GPU execution was performed. The Python check transcribed only dictionary normalization.

The parent tree contains Gemma3 definitions but no literal mm_input_projection occurrence. The author's Gemma3 motivation is therefore not independently verified against an affected checkpoint or a model-specific consumer.
Whole-tree searches located the direct read_header caller and all file_headers references; dynamic or external consumers remain unestablished.

chapters.title: Normalize the projector key before indexing tensors

claims.text: read_header first parses the JSON and records the payload start. It then collects matching key/value pairs before deleting and reinserting them, avoiding mutation during dictionary iteration. The original descriptor is reused unchanged.

The sole direct read_header caller found is SafetensorsCollection.add_tensor_files. Its additional name-fix check is redundant for this mapping because read_header has already removed the old key. The stored header and tensor_file_map nevertheless agree, preserving the existing size, listing and tensor-read interfaces.

A bounded standard-library transcription verified descriptor identity and payload-offset preservation, idempotence, and the collision rule: if both spellings exist, the legacy spelling's descriptor replaces the canonical descriptor. This checks dictionary semantics, not repository I/O.

findings.description: Normalization silently collapses two distinct header entries when both spellings exist.
findings.trigger: A scanned safetensors header contains both mapped spellings with different descriptors.
findings.expected_behavior: An ambiguous collision should be rejected or explicitly resolved rather than silently discarding the canonical descriptor.
findings.actual_behavior: read_header deletes the legacy key and unconditionally overwrites the canonical key with its descriptor. Collection override accounting cannot report this within-header collision because it sees only the normalized header.

verification.description: Transcribed normalization selected the legacy descriptor when both keys were supplied.
verification.limits: Synthetic dictionary only; no affected checkpoint established. Reach is the inspected add_tensor_files → read_header path, not a demonstrated model failure.

annotation.summary: Normalizes one Gemma3-related projector tensor spelling in parsed safetensors headers, keeping collection indexing and descriptor lookup consistent.
